title: AuthFly IdP
summary: SAML 2.0 + OIDC Identity Provider sharing one signed session.
hero: One IdP session for SAML and OIDC

sections.title: About this module
sections.body: Dual-protocol IdP written in Go: SAML AuthnRequest handling with ACS pinned to SP config, full OIDC authorization-code flow with JWKS, and a single signed idp_session cookie that bridges both protocols. Hanko provides credentials in the PoC; MVP swaps in Supabase or your own Postgres via the SSO SPI.

title: AuthKit
summary: Embeddable login, logout and error pages on Go + templ + UI8Kit.
hero: Hosted login UI, served from your origin

sections.title: About this module
sections.body: Implements Renderer (RenderLogin / RenderLogout / RenderError) and ships static assets via StaticFS(). Branding, FlowConfig and FeatureFlags come from the host app; AuthKit itself never imports a credential backend, so the same UI works against Hanko today and other providers tomorrow.

title: AuthKit TS
summary: TypeScript core for browser auth flows, with thin per-provider adapters.
hero: One core, many adapters — start with Hanko

sections.title: About this module
sections.body: The browser SDK core that AuthKit ships through SDKScript. A single TypeScript core handles flow orchestration; adapters bind it to a specific credential backend (Hanko first), so adding a new provider does not mean rewriting the UI or the IdP.

title: OIDC Hanko
summary: Hanko packaged as the PoC credential backend for Auth Fly.
hero: Hanko, ready for Auth Fly out of the box

sections.title: About this module
sections.body: Hanko Docker image and config tuned for the Auth Fly IdP: JWT + JWKS for browser sessions, cookie-bound tokens, and CORS aligned with the IdP origin. Implements core.CredentialVerifier so the rest of the stack stays provider-agnostic.

title: UI8Kit
summary: Component library that fully replaces Hanko Elements across the hosted UI.

sections.title: About this module
sections.body: UI8Kit is the component layer behind AuthKit: forms, fields, buttons, error states and the auth flow widgets. Bundled as a single ui8kit.js served from /static — no CDN dependency, no third-party JS in the login page.
